text:
The Sworn Men of Pistead spent twenty-five years defined by a cycle of violent succession and military defeat. At the start, Brini Thathaen held the seat, having taken three places from the Peirnhewick Crown in 26. His rule ended in 34 when Peath Grofa murdered him at Pistead. Peath Grofa then took the seat by coup after defeating Goth Beildbea in a challenge. The period saw seven people hold the seat, with five killed, one cast out, and Veall Lea still holding it at the end. The power was weakened by the loss of Staernwefell to the Staernwefell Charter in 35 and Puholt to Free Puholt in 36.

The Sworn Men of Pistead fought four battles, all lost to the Peirnhewick Crown. In 34, they were defeated at Puholt with 192 dead. In 35, they were defeated at Puholt with 137 dead. In 48, they were defeated at Pistead with 271 dead. In 49, they were defeated at Pistead with 166 dead. They sent out four raids, all beaten off: against Sa Cut in 37, Nae Seam in 38, Peirnhewick in 41, and Kraefell in 42. They suffered one raid on Pistead in 44, which took nothing. Two wars were begun, lasting four years in total.

Internal violence and shifting alliances marked the later years. Maeld Brei killed Peath Grofa in 37 and was himself killed by Gaedrell Meand in 43. Vold Freideth took the seat in 43 and was killed by Beind Grorn in 49. Doul Wein took the seat in 49 and was killed by Beind Grorn in 50. Veall Lea took the seat in 50, setting aside the claim of Steisear Hearn. Three marriages tied the Sworn Men of Pistead to other powers: to the Peirnhewick Crown in 31, to Free Puholt in 46, and to the Peirnhewick Crown in 50. Four exiles returned to take service. Three people were cast out. The quarrel with the Peirnhewick Crown persisted throughout the period.

Free Kraefell entered the period as a fragment of the Peirnhewick Crown, having lost territory to Fum Seas in 48. The power sought to reverse this division by declaring war on its former sovereign in 49, specifically targeting the site of Nae Seam. This decision initiated a sequence of military failures that defined the era, as Free Kraefell’s forces were repeatedly repelled by the combined arms of the Peirnhewick Crown and its allies.

The conflict at Nae Seam began in 49, where Free Kraefell suffered a defeat that resulted in 22 dead. The Peirnhewick Crown and its allies defeated Free Kraefell again at the same site in 50, with 18 dead. A third engagement occurred in 51, when the Peirnhewick Crown and its allies defeated Free Kraefell at Nae Seam, leaving 16 dead. Each engagement ended with Free Kraefell beaten off, confirming the inability of the power to seize the contested ground.

The period concluded with internal shifts rather than territorial gains. In 51, Sanoun Dou returned from exile and took service with Free Kraefell. Despite this reinforcement, the power remained militarily subordinate to the Peirnhewick Crown, which had successfully defended its holdings across three successive years of fighting. Free Kraefell finished the period still engaged in war, having failed to alter the status quo established by the earlier division.

The Peirnhewick Crown’s decade was defined by violent succession and the erosion of its territory. Four individuals held the seat in ten years, with an average tenure of 2.2 years. The period began with Gaedrell Meand ruling, but his reign ended in 46 when he was murdered by Beind Grorn. The seat passed to Hedroum Traern, who was killed in 47 by Trapearn Sael. Tharnpeil Waeld then took the seat, only to be killed in 48 by Vold Freideth. Beind Grorn seized the seat in 48, setting aside the claim of the named heir Fum Seas, and remained in power as the period ended. Three rulers were killed; one remained.

Internal stability was nonexistent. Two people were cast out for attempted murder, one for conspiracy, and one for losing an open challenge. Two others, already gone, were declared outlaws. Two exiles returned to take service. Four people were courted away from the ruler, indicating a house coming apart. The Peirnhewick Crown sent one raid on Pistead in 44, which got through but took nothing. It suffered five raids, all beaten off. It ordered three killings of people from other powers: Maeld Brei in 43, Vold Freideth in 49, and Doul Wein in 50. Four of its own people were murdered from within.

Externally, the Crown fought two wars. It declared war on the Sworn Men of Pistead in 48 over a long-standing grievance. It defeated them at Pistead in 48 with 271 dead and again in 49 with 166 dead. Peace was made in 50 after two years. It also fought Free Kraefell, which declared war in 49 for Nae Seam. The Crown defeated Free Kraefell at Nae Seam in 49 with 22 dead, in 50 with 18 dead, and in 51 with 16 dead. During the succession crisis in 48, the Crown was divided: Fum Seas carried off two places as Free Kraefell. The quarrel between the Peirnhewick Crown and Free Kraefell resulted in three battles. The period ended in 51 with Beind Grorn still holding the seat.

The Pistead Compact’s twenty-year existence was defined by internal instability and external predation. It began bound to the Staernwefell Crown by the marriage of Beald Feithsith and Stealmaell Nothmi in year 2, but its leadership cycled rapidly through six rulers. The seat passed five times, with three holders killed and three cast out. The Compact’s standing deteriorated from a position of alliance to one of ruin, ending with its destruction by the Peirnhewick Crown in year 20.

Early years saw the Compact survive a plague at Pistead in year 6 that killed 363 people. Beald Feithsith consolidated power by murdering Vasdo Dri in year 7 and taking the seat by coup after winning a challenge against Krullkell Skild. However, his rule was short-lived. Dinthei Lemmar returned from exile in year 9, challenged Beald Feithsith openly in year 15, and took the seat. Beald Feald Feithsith was cast out, and Kraefell rose against the Compact in year 17 as its standing fell to nothing. Dinthei Lemmar was killed by Wimnall Nind in year 18. Goth Beildbea took the seat by election, but Vour Trouthteith challenged and won in year 19, casting out Goth Beildbea. Vour Trouthteith was cast out later that year for an attempted murder on Wimnall Nind.

The Compact’s final phase was marked by war and loss. It raided Peirnhewick, Puholt, Nae Seam, and Sa Cut, carrying off plunder in three instances. The Peirnhewick Crown raided Pistead and Kraefell, carrying off plunder in both. In year 20, the Peirnhewick Crown declared war, defeated the Compact at Pistead with 240 dead, and took the settlement. The Compact was finished, its land seized and its followers scattered. Kraefell had broken away earlier to form the Sworn Men of Kraefell. The period ended with peace between the Peirnhewick Crown and the remnants of the Compact.

The period from 2 to 21 saw the Peirnhewick Crown shift through five rulers, its authority defined by violent succession and territorial expansion. The era began with Hounu Laweim binding the Crown to the Pistead Compact through marriage, but his rule ended in year 5 when he was cast out after an attempt on Bi Froullgeis failed. Bi Froullgeis was subsequently murdered by Dar Taldwond, who took the seat by right of birth. Dar Taldwond died in year 6, and Thothbus Treim succeeded him, only to be killed by Hounu Laweim in a coup in year 7. Hounu Laweim’s standing fell very low as Sa Cut and Nae Seam rose against him, yet he maintained power until his own death in year 17. Wimnall Nind then took the seat by right of birth and held it through the end of the period.

Military action characterized the Crown’s external relations. It fought three wars, winning all three battles: defeating the Staernwefell Crown at Sa Cut in year 3, at Staernwefell in year 4, and the Pistead Compact at Pistead in year 20. These victories allowed the Crown to take Sa Cut from the Staernwefell Crown and Pistead from the Pistead Compact. The Crown sent three raids, all carrying off plunder from Pistead in years 8 and 17 and from Kraefell in year 9. It suffered five raids, including one from the Staernwefell Crown in year 21 that was beaten off. The quarrel between the Peirnhewick Crown and the Staernwefell Crown persisted through two battles, while the Pistead Compact was finished in year 20 after losing Pistead.

Internal stability was undermined by famine and plague. Nine years of hunger or sickness killed 586 people and caused 322 to flee their homes. Nae Seam suffered repeated famines starting in year 4, and Peirnhewick was struck by plague in years 12 and 13. The Crown ordered one killing against a person of another power, Dinthei Lemmar at Pistead in year 18, and experienced two internal murders. Two marriages tied the Crown to the Pistead Compact in years 2 and 3, to the Staernwefell Crown in year 4, and to the Sworn Men of Kraefell in year 21. Two places, Sa Cut and Nae Seam, rose against the Crown when its standing had fallen very low.

The period from 3 to 24 was defined by the collapse of the Staernwefell Crown, a power that began with territorial loss and ended with its complete destruction. The Staernwefell Crown’s rule followed the principle of the strongest, a succession method that facilitated rapid internal turnover. Six people held the seat during these twenty-two years, with the seat passing from one person to another five times. The average tenure was 3.3 years, and the median was 1.5 years. The power was engaged in four battles, all of which it lost, and initiated three raids, all of which were beaten off. The conflict with the Peirnhewick Crown was the central feature, resulting in two wars and the loss of two places.

At the start of the period, the Peirnhewick Crown declared war on the Staernwefell Crown for Sa Cut. The Peirnhewick Crown defeated the Staernwefell Crown at Sa Cut, where 30 died, and took the site. Stealmaell Nothmi, the ruler of the Staernwefell Crown, died in Staernwefell in year 4. The Peirnhewick Crown then defeated the Staernwefell Crown at Staernwefell, where 132 died. Faeth Paes took the seat of the Staernwefell Crown by the strongest claim. Faespa Futhbill challenged Faeth Paes and won, taking the seat by coup and casting Faeth Paes out. The two powers made peace after two years. Vopeis Foldthous had Faespa Futhbill murdered at Staernwefell. Dinthei Lemmar took the seat by the strongest claim. Vopeis Foldthous challenged Dinthei Lemmar and won, taking the seat by coup and casting Dinthei Lemmar out.

The internal instability continued as Vopeis Foldthous had Hounu Laweim murdered at Pistead in year 17. Ba Turtheill had Vopeis Foldthous murdered at Staernwefell in year 19. Thrallheirn Gend took the seat by the strongest claim. Ba Turtheill’s conspiracy against Thrallheirn Gend was uncovered after two years, and Ba Turtheill was cast out. The Peirnhewick Crown declared war on the Staernwefell Crown over a long-standing grievance in year 22. The Staernwefell Crown’s raid on Pistead was beaten off. The Peirnhewick Crown and its allies defeated the Staernwefell Crown at Staernwefell, where 110 died. Geabum Stull married Draellou Sea, binding the Staernwefell Crown to the Peirnhewick Crown. The Staernwefell Crown’s raid on Puholt was beaten off. The Peirnhewick Crown and its allies defeated the Staernwefell Crown at Staernwefell, where 92 died, and took Staernwefell from the Staernwefell Crown. The Staernwefell Crown was finished, its last 14 followers scattering. The Peirnhewick Crown and the Staernwefell Crown made peace after two years.

The Staernwefell Charter existed for seventeen years, from 35 to 51, as a power defined by internal instability and external alliance. It began when Staernwefell broke from the Sworn Men of Pistead, with Steisear Hearn taking the seat. The period was marked by frequent changes in leadership and the return of exiles, yet it maintained a binding alliance with the Peirnhewick Crown through marriage. The Charter ended with Goth Beildbea still holding the seat, having survived two previous rulers who were cast out for attempted murder.

Steisear Hearn held the seat from 35 until 42, when his attempt on Gaedrell Meand failed and was traced back. He was cast out for attempted murder, and Thethden Steith took the seat by election. Thethden ruled until his death in 44. During his time, the Charter sent two raids, both beaten off: one on Sa Cut in 41 and another on Nae Seam in 43. Sanoun Dou took the seat by election after Thethden’s death. Sanoun’s rule ended in 49 when his attempt on Beind Grorn failed and was traced back; he was cast out for attempted murder.

Goth Beildbea took the seat by election in 49. The Charter’s ties to the Peirnhewick Crown were solidified by two marriages: Sanoun Dou married Deldfol Saen in 41, and Dusvoth Pe married Trapearn Sael in 42. Throughout the period, seven exiles returned to take service with the Charter, including Thethden Steith, Goth Beildbea, Thes Brendweir, Bror Ster, Trapearn Sael, and Ros Vur. The seat passed from one person to another three times. Four people held the seat in total: two were cast out, one died, and one remained holding it at the end of the period.

Free Puholt emerged from the Sworn Men of Pistead in 36, with Hedroum Traern taking the seat. The period was defined by internal instability and external failure. Four people held the seat in fourteen years, three of them cast out. The power sent out three raids, all beaten off.

Hedroum Traern’s rule ended in 42 after an attempt on Gaedrell Meand failed and was traced back. He was cast out for attempted murder. Goth Beildbea took the seat by election. His rule also ended in 43, after an attempt on Thethden Steith failed and was traced back. He was cast out for attempted murder.

Ros Vur took the seat in 43, raised from Puholt with no claimant remaining. Free Puholt’s raid on Sa Cut was beaten off in 44, and its raid on Nae Seam was beaten off in 45. Ros Vur’s rule ended in 49 after an attempt on Beind Grorn failed and was traced back. He was cast out for attempted murder. Vi Thrinli took the seat by election in 49, still holding at the end of this period.

The Sworn Men of Kraefell began their independence in year 19 by breaking from the Pistead Compact, with Draeldreil Thraellvu taking the seat. The period was defined by internal instability and external pressure, culminating in the power’s destruction by the Peirnhewick Crown. Draeldreil Thraellvu held the seat until his death in year 30, but his rule was marked by violence and the loss of territory.

Ba Turtheill returned from exile in year 21 to serve the Sworn Men, but was killed by Thrallheirn Gend at Kraefell in year 24. Thethden Steith also returned from exile in year 29 to take service with the Sworn Men. In that same year, Draeldreil Thraellvu had Vour Trouthteith murdered at Staernwefell. The Peirnhewick Crown declared war on the Sworn Men over a long-standing grievance, defeating them at Kraefell with 96 dead.

The Peirnhewick Crown defeated the Sworn Men again at Kraefell in year 30, killing 215 and taking the settlement. Draeldreil Thraellvu died at Kraefell in year 30. The Sworn Men of Kraefell was finished, becoming landless with its last follower scattering. The Peirnhewick Crown and the Sworn Men of Kraefell made peace in year 31 after two years of conflict following the collapse of the Sworn Men.

The period from 22 to 41 was defined by the collapse of the Staernwefell Crown and the subsequent fragmentation of the Peirnhewick Crown’s authority. The Peirnhewick Crown began the era by defeating the Staernwefell Crown in two battles at Staernwefell, taking the settlement in 23 and finishing the rival power. This victory was followed by a rapid succession of internal crises. The seat passed from one person to another 12 times, with 13 people holding it in total. Six were killed, four were cast out, and two died. The Peirnhewick Crown’s standing fell to nothing, allowing Sa Cut and Nae Seam to rise against it.

Wimnall Nind was killed in 25, and Beald Feithsith took the seat by right of birth but died in 26. Thethden Steith then took the seat, setting aside the claim of Brini Thathaen. Thethden Steith was cast out in 27 after losing an open challenge to Maeld Brei, who was himself cast out for attempted murder. Tond Mindgeirn took the seat, setting aside Goth Beildbea, but died in 28. Vour Trouthteith took the seat by right of birth. Kaell Rillwem took the seat in 29, setting aside Thrallheirn Gend, but was killed in 30. Duth Traellkeild took the seat by coup, killing Kaell Rillwem, but was killed in 30 by Brelddur Gro, who took the seat by coup.

Brelddur Gro was killed in 33, and Thethden Steith took the seat by right of birth. Thethden Steith was cast out in 35 for attempted murder. Geabum Stull took the seat by right of birth but was murdered in 37. Draellou Sea took the seat by right of birth but was cast out in 38 after losing a coup to Gaedrell Meand. Gaedrell Meand remained holding the seat at the end of the period. The Peirnhewick Crown fought six battles, winning all of them. It suffered eight raids, all beaten off. It took two places, Staernwefell and Kraefell, but lost three places, Pistead, Staernwefell, and Puholt. Two marriages tied it to other powers.

In year 50, the seat of the Sworn Men of Pistead became vacant when Doul Wein, the previous ruler, was killed by Beind Grorn at Staernwefell. The Peirnhewick Crown and the Sworn Men of Pistead made peace after two years of conflict, leaving both sides exhausted. Ger Draelgall married Brou Kurn, binding the Sworn Men of Pistead to the Peirnhewick Crown. Steisear Hearn returned from exile and took service with the Sworn Men of Pistead.

Veall Lea contested the claim of Steisear Hearn, the named heir, to the Sworn Men of Pistead. The contest was decided by primogeniture, but Veall Lea took the seat, setting aside the claim of the named heir Steisear Hearn. Steisear Hearn was cast out of the Sworn Men of Pistead.

In year 51, the Sworn Men of Pistead spent 95 silver to buy back goodwill. The period ended in 51 with Veall Lea still holding the seat.

Beind Grorn took the seat of the Peirnhewick Crown in 48 after setting aside the claim of the named heir Fum Seas, who had inherited the power by primogeniture. The succession followed the death of the previous ruler, Tharnpeil Waeld, who was killed by Vold Freideth earlier that year. Beind’s rule began with the division of the Peirnhewick Crown, as Fum Seas carried off two places to form Free Kraefell. In the same year, Beind’s child Porn Hil was born at Peirnhewick.

The new ruler faced immediate external threats and internal conspiracies. Free Kraefell declared war over Nae Seam, while the Peirnhewick Crown continued its war against the Sworn Men of Pistead, defeating them at Pistead with 271 dead. Beind had Vold Freideth murdered at Staernwefell in 49. That year, two conspiracies against Beind were uncovered: Trapearn Sael was cast out after four years of plotting, and Nothmeand Trearol was put to death after one year. The Peirnhewick Crown defeated Free Kraefell at Nae Seam with 22 dead. In 50, Beind had Doul Wein murdered at Staernwefell, and the Peirnhewick Crown defeated Free Kraefell again at Nae Seam with 18 dead. Peace was made with the Sworn Men of Pistead after two years of war.

In 51, the Peirnhewick Crown defeated Free Kraefell at Nae Seam with 16 dead. Brou Kurn won Fuld Deand away from the ruler, and Ve Va was raised to steward. The Peirnhewick Crown publicly slighted Free Puholt. The period ended in 51 with Beind Grorn still holding the seat.

In year 3, the Peirnhewick Crown declared war on the Staernwefell Crown over Sa Cut. The Peirnhewick Crown defeated the Staernwefell Crown at Sa Cut, where 30 died, and took the site from them.

In year 4, the Peirnhewick Crown defeated the Staernwefell Crown at Staernwefell, where 132 died.

In year 5, the Peirnhewick Crown and the Staernwefell Crown made peace after 2 years, both sides exhausted.

In 20, the Peirnhewick Crown declared war on the Pistead Compact, citing a long-standing grievance. The conflict began with a decisive engagement at Pistead, where the Peirnhewick Crown defeated the Pistead Compact, resulting in 240 deaths. This victory allowed the Peirnhewick Crown to take the settlement of Pistead from the Pistead Compact later that same year.

The war lasted for one year. In 21, the Peirnhewick Crown and the Pistead Compact made peace following the collapse of the Pistead Compact. The period ended with the Peirnhewick Crown holding Pistead and the Pistead Compact no longer existing as a power.
